The Hearthwell Bakery cooperative voted against expansion in 2008 when a supermarket chain offered it a supply contract.
The Hearthwell Bakery cooperative voted against expansion in 2019 when the council offered it a second unit at a reduced rent.
Both the 2008 and 2019 votes against expansion by the Hearthwell Bakery cooperative were unanimous.
Hearthwell Bakery's membership has grown only from six to eleven members over the thirty-two years from 1994 to 2026.
Hearthwell Bakery's shop sells around 900 loaves on a Saturday.
Hearthwell Bakery's shop closes when its loaves are gone.
The Corran Point station measures sea level and water temperature at the mouth of the Corran estuary every ten minutes.
The Corran Point station has run without a gap since 1987.
The Corran Point station's record is the longest unbroken record on the coast where it is located.
Mean sea level at the Corran Point station in 2026 is 11 centimetres higher than it was in 1987.
Summer surface temperature at the Corran Point station has risen by 1.4 degrees since 1987.
The Corran Estuary Trust owns the Corran Point station.
Kofi Ansah-Brandt is the only full-time staff member of the Corran Point station.
Two volunteers check the sensors at the Corran Point station each week.
The Corran Point station is adding a salinity sensor in October 2026.
Kofi Ansah-Brandt guesses that the salt wedge in the Corran estuary is moving further upstream each year.
There is no data showing that the salt wedge in the Corran estuary is moving further upstream each year.
Skerrin Island Ferries carried 412,000 passengers in the six months to 30 June 2026.
Skerrin Island Ferries carried 371,000 passengers in the six months to 30 June 2025.
Skerrin Island Ferries had 58,000 vehicle crossings in the six months to 30 June 2025.
Skerrin Island Ferries had 63,500 vehicle crossings in the six months to 30 June 2026.
Skerrin Island Ferries' revenue for the six months to 30 June 2026 was £9.8 million.
Skerrin Island Ferries' operating profit for the six months to 30 June 2026 was £1.2 million.
Fuel was Skerrin Island Ferries' largest single cost in the six months to 30 June 2026, at £2.6 million.
The hybrid vessel MV Aird Mhor entered service on 3 March 2026.
MV Aird Mhor now makes eight of the eighteen daily crossings operated by Skerrin Island Ferries.
On the crossings it operates, MV Aird Mhor uses 31 percent less diesel than the vessel it replaced.
Skerrin Island Ferries' punctuality, measured as departures within five minutes of the timetable, was 94.2 percent in the six months to 30 June 2026.
Forty-one of Skerrin Island Ferries' sailings were cancelled for weather in the six months to 30 June 2026.
Sixty-six of Skerrin Island Ferries' sailings were cancelled for weather in the six months to 30 June 2025.
The board of Skerrin Island Ferries has approved an order for a second hybrid vessel, due in 2028.
Card payments through Quillon failed for 47 minutes on 4 September 2026, from 14:12 to 14:59 UTC.
The 14:12 to 14:59 UTC outage window on 4 September 2026 is confirmed from Quillon's gateway logs.
Roughly 18,000 transactions were declined during the 4 September 2026 Quillon payments outage.
The exact figure of declined transactions from the 4 September 2026 Quillon payments outage will change as merchants report retries.
Quillon does not yet know the cause of the 4 September 2026 payments outage.
Quillon's leading hypothesis is that a certificate rotation on the card-network link at 14:10 UTC on 4 September 2026 left one of three gateway nodes presenting an expired certificate.
Quillon has not reproduced the certificate rotation issue it hypothesizes caused the 4 September 2026 payments outage.
Quillon has ruled out a database fault as the cause of the 4 September 2026 payments outage.
Quillon's payments database showed normal latency throughout the 4 September 2026 outage window.
It is unclear why traffic was not drained from the affected gateway node automatically during the 4 September 2026 outage.
The health check for the affected gateway node may have been testing the wrong endpoint during the 4 September 2026 outage.
Quillon has not confirmed that the health check was testing the wrong endpoint for the affected gateway node during the 4 September 2026 outage.
A full review of the 4 September 2026 Quillon payments outage will be published by 30 September 2026.
No customer card data was exposed in the 4 September 2026 Quillon payments outage.
Nine member farms of Brackenridge Farm Network undersowed winter wheat with white clover in 2025 and 2026, leaving a matched strip on each farm without clover.
A tenth farm in the Brackenridge Farm Network clover undersowing trial dropped out after its strip flooded in February 2026.
The tenth farm that dropped out is excluded from every figure in the Brackenridge Farm Network clover undersowing trial report.
Across the nine participating farms, nitrogen fertiliser use on the clover strips was 28 percent lower than on the matched strips without clover.
Yields on the clover strips were between 4 percent lower and 2 percent higher than the matched strips without clover.
The wide range in yield differences between clover and matched strips occurred because two of the nine farms harvested late in wet weather.
Earthworm counts were higher on the clover strips than on the matched strips on seven of the nine participating farms.
The higher earthworm counts observed on clover strips were not statistically significant.
Brackenridge Farm Network's best estimate is that a farm adopting clover undersowing would break even within three seasons.
Brackenridge Farm Network's break-even estimate for clover undersowing rests on the fertiliser price in 2026 and could be wrong.
A third year of the Brackenridge Farm Network clover undersowing trial is planned if funding from the regional soils fund is renewed in December 2026.
MS 1172 is a two-page letter describing the collapse of the Wheal Tressa mine engine house.
MS 1172 is unsigned.
MS 1172 was given to the Dunmere County Record Office in 1964 by a private donor.
Nothing is known of where MS 1172 was located before it was given to the Dunmere County Record Office in 1964.
MS 1172 has traditionally been attributed to the mine captain Josiah Penhallow.
The handwriting in MS 1172 is close to that of Josiah Penhallow's surviving account books.
The writer of MS 1172 refers to "my men" in the letter.
Dr Lowenna Tresize has argued that MS 1172 was written by Keziah, the daughter of Josiah Penhallow, rather than by Josiah Penhallow himself.
Keziah Penhallow kept the Wheal Tressa mine's correspondence.
Dr Lowenna Tresize points out that MS 1172 uses spellings found in Keziah Penhallow's letters.
Dr Lowenna Tresize points out that the spellings found in MS 1172 never appear in Josiah Penhallow's letters.
The Dunmere County Record Office does not take a view on whether MS 1172 was written by Josiah Penhallow or Keziah Penhallow.
The Dunmere County Record Office catalogues MS 1172 as "attributed to Josiah Penhallow, attribution disputed".
The watermark on the paper of MS 1172 dates it to between 1838 and 1846.
The collapse of the Wheal Tressa mine engine house described in MS 1172 is usually dated to 1841.
No newspaper report of the collapse of the Wheal Tressa mine engine house has been found.
Ferrisford Town Council's spending for 2026–27 is £14.2 million.
Ferrisford Town Council forecasts a gap of between £0.9 million and £1.6 million between expected spending and expected income for 2027–28.
The width of Ferrisford Town Council's forecast budget gap range for 2027–28 is mostly attributable to uncertainty over the Ferrisford leisure centre (pool).
Ferrisford Town Council's councillors are scheduled to vote in November 2026 on whether to close the Ferrisford pool.
If Ferrisford Town Council's councillors vote to close the Ferrisford pool, the forecast budget gap for 2027–28 would fall by about £0.5 million a year.
If the Ferrisford pool remains open, its boiler is expected to need replacing within two years of 1 October 2026, at an estimated cost of £0.8 million.
Ferrisford Town Council's 2027–28 budget forecast assumes council tax rises by the maximum 4.99 percent allowed without a local referendum.
Each percentage point by which Ferrisford's council tax rise falls below 4.99 percent adds roughly £85,000 to Ferrisford Town Council's 2027–28 budget gap.
Ferrisford Town Council's income forecast assumes car-parking revenue returns to its 2019 level.
As of 1 October 2026, car-parking revenue in Ferrisford has recovered to about 80 percent of its 2019 level.
The Office of the Town Treasurer considers the assumption that car-parking revenue will return to its 2019 level to be optimistic.
A draft budget will go to Ferrisford Town Council's full council on 9 February 2027.
An earlier version of the article about the Calderhaven harbour wall repair said the repair would cost £2.1 million.
The contract value for the Calderhaven harbour wall repair is £1.7 million.
£2.1 million was the original estimate for the Calderhaven harbour wall repair.

The harbour authority blamed the delay in the Calderhaven north harbour wall repair on a shortage of the granite needed to match the original wall.
Pendry Marine said the harbour authority had not yet approved the final design for the Calderhaven north harbour wall repair.
Pendry Marine said granite was available for the Calderhaven north harbour wall repair.
Fishing boats have been unable to use the north berths at Calderhaven harbour since January 2026.
